findings.issue: Index 106 keys seven full-credit paths. Six are the same as in the other nine Hemoptoicos stories. The seventh is APARELHO HEMOLINFOPOIÉTICO > Hemorragias (“Sangramentos espontâneos ou desproporcionais a traumas.”), keyed because the utterance adds “Não havia machucado nem pancada antes disso”. The utterance itself places the blood after a cough (“depois que tossi”), does not say the bleeding was spontaneous, and describes a fine streak in phlegm, the finding the script names as Hemoptoicos. The same convention appears at index 95 of this batch (a Hemoptise story) and in three of the ten base Epistaxe stories; those items are outside this review.

evidence.quote: Hemorragias: Sangramentos espontâneos ou desproporcionais a traumas.
Hemoptoicos: escarro com pequenas estrias ou traços de sangue
Hemoptise: eliminação de muco ou escarro com sangue ao tossir

evidence.text: Vi sangue no muco que cuspi ao tossir, embora eu não tivesse levado pancada nem machucado a boca ou o nariz.

evidence.exampleText: Começou a sair sangue pela narina esquerda sem eu ter batido ou machucado o nariz. Precisei pegar um lenço para não sujar a roupa.

findings.resolution: Held under the instruction to hold when in doubt. The reviewer does not claim the path is wrong: the sentence does deny trauma, which is the letter of the description. The doubt is whether the general bleeding entry of the blood block should earn the same credit as Hemoptoicos for a fine streak brought up by coughing, and whether “no injury or blow” is the same as “spontaneous” when a cough is the stated antecedent. A teaching decision can clear it without rewording.
findings.requiredStoryChange: Not rewritten by the reviewer. Either record a teaching decision that Hemorragias is accepted here (then the key stays and the convention is confirmed for index 95 and the base Epistaxe stories as well), or remove Hemorragias from acceptedContextIds and acceptedPathEvidence and correct the story rationale. A re-mapped or reworded story needs a new independent review.

findings.issue: Indices 100–109 give full credit to Hemoptoicos and to Hemoptise. The script prints Hemoptise as “eliminação de muco ou escarro com sangue ao tossir” and Hemoptoicos as “escarro com pequenas estrias ou traços de sangue”: read literally, the first contains the second. All ten utterances describe only a small streak, dot or trace, and three explicitly deny a larger amount (101 “Não era sangue preenchendo o lenço”, 104 “não um volume de sangue separado”, 107 “O sangue era só aquele fio, não o catarro inteiro”). In the reverse direction the batch's Hemoptise stories key Hemoptoicos only when the streak is fine (indices 93 and 97) and write the others so that it is excluded (for example index 90, “Não era só um fio fino de sangue”).

evidence.quote: Hemoptise: eliminação de muco ou escarro com sangue ao tossir

evidence.text: Tossi e saiu um catarro com sangue misturado, bem avermelhado. Não era só um fio fino de sangue.
O catarro que veio quando tossi tinha só dois risquinhos finos de sangue. O resto da secreção estava claro.
Cuspi depois de tossir e encontrei um fiozinho de sangue dentro do catarro. Era só aquela linha vermelha fina.

findings.resolution: Passed. On the printed wording a student who answers Hemoptise for blood-streaked phlegm brought up by coughing is not wrong, and the key is applied the same way across the ten stories and the neighbouring Hemoptise stories. In common clinical usage the two terms are often separated by amount; if the teacher wants that separation, Hemoptise should be removed from these ten stories. Teaching confirmation recommended before clinical approval.

findings.issue: Indices 100–109 also give full credit to Expectoração and Tosse, each in two blocks (LARINGE/FARINGE and CARDIOVASCULAR): four of the six keyed paths. Every utterance does state a cough and mucus or phlegm brought up by it, so the four paths are supported by the printed descriptions. The effect is that a student who answers only “Tosse” to a sentence whose point is blood in the phlegm receives full credit.

findings.resolution: Passed. This is the batch's stated policy (all equally supported coherent paths receive full credit) and is applied consistently to the neighbouring Expectoração and Hemoptise stories (index 80 shown as example). The cardiovascular heading only locates the homonymous entries; no cardiac cause is implied. Whether the less specific terms should earn the same credit as the specific one is a scoring decision for the teacher.

findings.issue: Index 100 never says “sangue”: the finding is “um risquinho vermelho bem fino”. Index 104 says “tracinhos vermelhos” and names blood only in the denial that follows. Indices 105 and 108 describe dots (“um ponto”, “alguns pontinhos … espalhados”), not streaks; 108 is the largest amount in the group. Index 106 says “catarro e uma estria fina de sangue”, coordinating the two instead of placing the streak in the phlegm. Indices 112 (“som agudo”) and 117 (“som fino”) have no whistle comparison; 115 says “som musical fino”. Indices 112 and 119 use the source's own adjective “agudo”, and 119 also “assovio”, as the clue.
findings.resolution: None of these opens another term. Red in phlegm is read as blood (the reviewer found no other script entry for it), dots are traces, and “fino”/“agudo” in the chest with breathing has no competing entry. Suggested polish for a later edit: say “de sangue” at index 100; at 106 write that the streak was in the phlegm; add a whistle or kettle comparison at 112 and 117.

findings.issue: The twenty story rationales are story-specific and name only keyed terms or none; in each story the evidence rationale of the primary path repeats the story rationale. The 51 evidence rationales of the secondary paths (Hemoptise, Expectoração, Tosse, Hemorragias) are one stock sentence, “O relato explicita a manifestação definida em <termo>: <descrição> A posição no roteiro não define etiologia.”, with no full stop after the pasted description except for Hemorragias. Details: index 115 says “pela paciente e acompanhante”, although the utterance does not give the speaker's sex, and “agudo” where the utterance says “fino”; index 110 says “sincronizado à expiração”, which is more technical than the utterance; indices 103 and 109 do not name any term; index 105 says “ambos os termos sanguinolentos” without naming them; index 100 calls a streak described only as red “estria sanguínea”.
findings.resolution: No rationale names a symptom or term that belongs to another group: there is no copy-paste leftover. The stock sentences are generic and badly punctuated rather than wrong. Passing stories are not held for this. Since the app may show the rationale to the student, the stock sentences should be replaced by story-specific ones in a later edit, and the gendered wording at 115 corrected. The rationale gap at index 106 is part of B023-01.

items.reasoning: Os seis caminhos respiratórios e cardiovasculares são sustentados: depois de tossir, o lenço ficou “com catarro e uma estria fina de sangue” — Hemoptoicos, com Hemoptise pela redação ampla (B023-02), Expectoração e Tosse. A dúvida está no sétimo caminho. Esta é a única das dez falas que dá crédito integral a Hemorragias (APARELHO HEMOLINFOPOIÉTICO: “Sangramentos espontâneos ou desproporcionais a traumas.”), com base na segunda frase: “Não havia machucado nem pancada antes disso”. Lida ao pé da letra, a frase nega trauma. Mas não consigo confirmar que isso baste: (a) a própria fala dá um antecedente imediato para o sangue, a tosse (“depois que tossi”), de modo que “espontâneo” não está dito, apenas “sem machucado nem pancada”; (b) a entrada está no bloco do sangue e, na minha leitura, descreve tendência a sangrar; uma estria fina no catarro é o achado que a apostila já nomeia como Hemoptoicos, e dar a Hemorragias o mesmo crédito ensina que qualquer traço de sangue sem trauma é “hemorragia”; (c) as outras nove falas do grupo descrevem o mesmo achado e não aceitam Hemorragias — a diferença é só a frase negativa. O lote usa a mesma convenção no índice 95 e a base em três histórias de Epistaxe (não revisadas aqui); isso mostra que a escolha é deliberada, não que esteja certa. Pela regra de reter na dúvida, o item fica retido para decisão docente. Observação secundária: “catarro e uma estria fina de sangue” coordena os dois em vez de dizer que a estria estava no catarro; leio como a mesma secreção no lenço (B023-04).

If yes, record the decision and keep the key; if no, remove Hemorragias from acceptedContextIds/acceptedPathEvidence and correct the story rationale.
